sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: As of 30 April 2026, the programme has successfully migrated 68% of targeted production workloads to Azure and AWS environments, exceeding the Q2 milestone by 9 percentage points. The accelerated cutover of customer analytics, HRIS, and three regional web portals has materially reduced our on‑premises data centre footprint. Run‑rate cloud spend is currently 14.7% below the FY2024 on‑prem baseline when adjusted for growth in transaction volumes. Overall programme health remains rated Green, with no critical path slippage.

sections.heading: Workload Migration Progress
sections.body: During April, 37 additional virtual machines and 12 database instances were decommissioned from the Milton Keynes and Brno data centres following successful cloud cutover. Application wave 2B, including the Claims Adjudication platform and Document Imaging service, completed performance validation with zero Priority 1 incidents. Remaining legacy UNIX workloads (8 servers) are now scheduled for migration in June, pending final middleware compatibility testing. Data replication lag has been reduced to under 120 milliseconds through network optimisation and ExpressRoute bandwidth scaling.

sections.heading: Cost Optimisation and Financial Position
sections.body: Total monthly cloud operating expenditure for April closed at £1.84m, compared to the adjusted on‑prem baseline of £2.16m for equivalent capacity and usage. Savings have been driven by reserved instance commitments for compute (three‑year term) and rightsizing of overprovisioned SQL clusters, delivering £210k in recurring monthly efficiency gains. Storage lifecycle policies introduced in March have shifted 42 TB to archival tiers, reducing storage costs by 23% without affecting retrieval SLAs. Finance has validated that cumulative net savings since programme inception now stand at £3.9m.

sections.heading: Operational Readiness and Risk Management
sections.body: The Cloud Operations team completed 24x7 support readiness drills, achieving a 96% success rate in simulated incident response scenarios. Updated runbooks for Kubernetes cluster failover and IAM access recertification have been approved and published in the ServiceNow knowledge base. Two moderate risks remain open: dependency on a legacy licensing model for the Policy Engine and skills gaps in Terraform automation within the regional IT teams. Mitigation actions include vendor renegotiation workshops and a targeted enablement bootcamp scheduled for late May.

sections.heading: Next-Phase Planning (Wave 3)
sections.body: Wave 3 planning has been baselined to commence on 1 July 2026, focusing on core finance systems and the enterprise data warehouse. A detailed application rationalisation review identified 11 redundant services to be retired rather than migrated, improving projected ROI by 6%. Network segmentation design and zero‑trust security controls are being finalised to support sensitive financial workloads. The Steering Committee is requested to approve the £4.2m capital allocation for Wave 3 by 20 May to maintain deployment momentum.

structure.full_text:
Cloud Migration Programme Status Report – Wave 2 Acceleration
Ref: CMP-2101525 | Date: 04 May 2026 | From: Elena Kovács, Director of Cloud Transformation | To: Executive Steering Committee

Section Executive Summary
As of 30 April 2026, the programme has successfully migrated 68% of targeted production workloads to Azure and AWS environments, exceeding the Q2 milestone by 9 percentage points. The accelerated cutover of customer analytics, HRIS, and three regional web portals has materially reduced our on‑premises data centre footprint. Run‑rate cloud spend is currently 14.7% below the FY2024 on‑prem baseline when adjusted for growth in transaction volumes. Overall programme health remains rated Green, with no critical path slippage.

Section Workload Migration Progress
During April, 37 additional virtual machines and 12 database instances were decommissioned from the Milton Keynes and Brno data centres following successful cloud cutover. Application wave 2B, including the Claims Adjudication platform and Document Imaging service, completed performance validation with zero Priority 1 incidents. Remaining legacy UNIX workloads (8 servers) are now scheduled for migration in June, pending final middleware compatibility testing. Data replication lag has been reduced to under 120 milliseconds through network optimisation and ExpressRoute bandwidth scaling.

Section Cost Optimisation and Financial Position
Total monthly cloud operating expenditure for April closed at £1.84m, compared to the adjusted on‑prem baseline of £2.16m for equivalent capacity and usage. Savings have been driven by reserved instance commitments for compute (three‑year term) and rightsizing of overprovisioned SQL clusters, delivering £210k in recurring monthly efficiency gains. Storage lifecycle policies introduced in March have shifted 42 TB to archival tiers, reducing storage costs by 23% without affecting retrieval SLAs. Finance has validated that cumulative net savings since programme inception now stand at £3.9m.

Section Operational Readiness and Risk Management
The Cloud Operations team completed 24x7 support readiness drills, achieving a 96% success rate in simulated incident response scenarios. Updated runbooks for Kubernetes cluster failover and IAM access recertification have been approved and published in the ServiceNow knowledge base. Two moderate risks remain open: dependency on a legacy licensing model for the Policy Engine and skills gaps in Terraform automation within the regional IT teams. Mitigation actions include vendor renegotiation workshops and a targeted enablement bootcamp scheduled for late May.

Section Next-Phase Planning (Wave 3)
Wave 3 planning has been baselined to commence on 1 July 2026, focusing on core finance systems and the enterprise data warehouse. A detailed application rationalisation review identified 11 redundant services to be retired rather than migrated, improving projected ROI by 6%. Network segmentation design and zero‑trust security controls are being finalised to support sensitive financial workloads. The Steering Committee is requested to approve the £4.2m capital allocation for Wave 3 by 20 May to maintain deployment momentum.

Confidential — Internal Distribution Only | Page 1 of 2
